mainPoints.explanation: By fine-tuning a Qwen-3.5-35B model with LoRA SFT, LangChain achieved accuracy comparable to or exceeding GPT-4 and Claude Opus on both in-domain and out-of-domain datasets.
mainPoints.point: A fine-tuned Qwen model can match frontier model performance on the 'Perceived Error' classification task.

mainPoints.explanation: The cost savings are significant, especially as trace volumes grow. The fine-tuned model's lower inference cost enables processing every production trace, not just a sample.
mainPoints.point: The fine-tuned model is 10-100x cheaper to serve than frontier models, making it viable for high-volume trace analysis.

mainPoints.explanation: A model trained solely on chat-langchain data transferred effectively to the Fleet dataset, outperforming all frontier models. This suggests the signal is universal and not application-specific.
mainPoints.point: The 'Perceived Error' judge generalizes well across different agent applications.

mainPoints.explanation: The team hypothesized that the key signals for perceived error are in the conversational turns, not the tool calls. This choice simplified the input and proved effective.
mainPoints.point: The data preparation process prioritized human and AI messages over tool calls for the classification task.

oneSentenceSummary: LangChain partnered with Fireworks to fine-tune a Qwen model as a 'Perceived Error' judge for production traces, achieving frontier-level accuracy at up to 100x lower cost.
originalTitle: Building a 100x Cheaper Trace Judge with Fireworks
summary: This article details a collaboration between LangChain and Fireworks to build a cost-effective 'Trace Judge' for mining signals from production agent traces. The core idea is to detect 'Perceived Error'—when a user believes the assistant made a mistake—a general-purpose signal applicable across applications. The team fine-tuned a Qwen-3.5-35B model using LoRA SFT on Fireworks, training it on data from one internal dataset (chat-langchain) and testing its transferability to another (Fleet). Results show the fine-tuned model matches or exceeds frontier models (like GPT-4 and Claude Opus) in accuracy, while being 10-100x cheaper to serve. The article also discusses the data preparation process, the use of model-assisted labeling with human review, and future research directions for trace understanding and continual learning.
title: Building a 100x Cheaper Trace Judge with Fireworks
